name: CO-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+20 partisan lean gives Democrats a structural advantage
Neguse's $3.1 million cash on hand against a Republican challenger with no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 95 percent

model.rationale: A D+20 district, a heavily funded incumbent, and market pricing near 95 percent Democratic all point the same direction, and nothing in the record suggests a competitive race. The main uncertainty is the size of the margin, not the winner.
model.watch: Only a major scandal or a historic national backlash could narrow the margin, since no recent environment has come close to erasing a 20-point district lean.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Joe Neguse, the Democratic incumbent, seeks re-election in a Colorado district that leans 20 points Democratic. He has raised $2.7 million and holds $3.1 million on hand, while Republican Kelley Dennison shows no reported fundraising. A Libertarian is also on the ballot. No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the picture rests on district partisanship, incumbency, and the large money gap.

Prediction markets put Democratic odds around 95 percent, in line with the seat's strong Democratic fundamentals. A Republican victory would require a swing far beyond anything seen in recent Colorado elections. The expected outcome is a comfortable double-digit Democratic win, with the open question being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
